translationRepairs: For merit he received the brevet rank of Right Censor-in-Chief, was promoted to deputy commander at Chengdu, and then to brigadier at Chongqing.
For merit he received the brevet rank of Right Dudu (Right Commander-in-Chief), was promoted to deputy commander at Chengdu, and then to brigadier at Chongqing.
右都督 is the military rank Right Dudu, not the censorial office 右都御史.
His merit was recorded; he was given the brevet rank of Right Censor-in-Chief, was promoted to deputy commander at Chengdu, and was transferred to brigadier at Chongqing.
His merit was recorded; he was given the brevet rank of Right Dudu, was promoted to deputy commander at Chengdu, and was transferred to brigadier at Chongqing.
The literal field contains the same conflation of 右都督 with a censorial office.

Funeral honors were long delayed. In Kangxi 22 (1683) he was granted sacrificial burial, given the posthumous title Zhongmin (Loyal and Sorrowful), and awarded the combined hereditary ranks of Baturu Bannerman and Tosaha Bannerman.

Funeral honors were long delayed. In Kangxi 22 (1683) he was granted sacrificial burial, given the posthumous title Zhongmin (Loyal and Sorrowful), and awarded the combined hereditary ranks of baitalabulehafan and tuoshalahafan.
拜他喇布勒哈番 and 拖沙喇哈番 are hereditary Manchu ranks; the existing 'Baturu Bannerman' wording identifies neither rank correctly.

The Emperor replaced him with Zhao Liangdong, seized Xiong Hu, the ringleader platoon commander Liu De, and all the soldiers who had killed Fu, and executed them. Fu was posthumously made a third-rank duke with a hereditary third-rank Jingni Bannerman title and given the posthumous name Zhongmin (Loyal and Sorrowful).

The Emperor replaced him with Zhao Liangdong, seized Xiong Hu, the ringleader platoon commander Liu De, and all the soldiers who had killed Fu, and executed them. Fu was posthumously made a third-rank duke with a hereditary third-rank jingqinihafan title and given the posthumous name Zhongmin (Loyal and Sorrowful).
精奇尼哈番 is a hereditary Manchu rank and is not accurately rendered as 'Jingni Bannerman.'
In Kangxi 11 (1672) he was made Grain Intendant of Suzhou and Songjiang.
In Shunzhi 11 (1654) he was made Grain Intendant of Suzhou and Songjiang.
The surrounding chronology runs from Shunzhi 4 through year 11 and then to Kangxi 3, so 十一年 is Shunzhi 11 (1654).
They set out a great basin of wine laced with poison. Liu and twenty-one servants and maids who drank included
They set out a great basin of wine laced with poison. Liu and the serving women and maids who drank numbered twenty-one.
The existing English ends mid-clause. The source states that Liu and the attendants who drank numbered twenty-one.
They slashed Yongsheng's arm, seized his seal, wounded his foot and servants, and dragged Yingliu to the horse-review ground.
They slashed Yongsheng's arm, seized his seal, wounded his foot again; he fell. They then dragged Yingliu to the horse-review ground.
僕 is the verb 'to fall' here, following the renewed wound to Yongsheng's foot; it does not introduce servants as another object of the attack.
